title: 1994 FIFA World Cup Final
content: The 1994 FIFA World Cup final in Pasadena saw Brazil beat Italy in a penalty shootout after a 0-0 draw, securing Brazil's fourth title.

title: Brazil Campaign 1994
content: Brazil went undefeated through the 1994 World Cup, winning the final on penalties, with stars like Romario, Bebeto, and captain Dunga leading the team.

title: Italy Campaign 1994
content: Italy reached the 1994 final with a disciplined defense led by Paolo Maldini and Roberto Baggio, but lost to Brazil on penalties after the match finished 0-0.

title: 1994 FIFA World Cup Host
content: The 1994 FIFA World Cup was hosted by the United States and featured matches in venues from Pasadena to Orlando, boosting soccer interest across America.

title: Golden Boot and Key Players 1994
content: Hristo Stoichkov shared the Golden Boot with Oleg Salenko at the 1994 World Cup, while Romario was voted the best player for his forward play.

title: 1994 Final Penalty Shootout
content: The penalty shootout in the 1994 final ended 3-2 in favor of Brazil after goalkeeper Cláudio Taffarel saved two shots and Roberto Baggio missed the decisive kick.

title: 1994 World Cup Legacy in USA
content: Hosting the 1994 FIFA World Cup led to a surge of interest in soccer in the US and paved the way for Major League Soccer's launch in 1996.

title: 1994 Quarterfinal Overview
content: Germany, Bulgaria, Sweden, and Brazil made the quarterfinals in 1994, with Brazil defeating Sweden 1-0 thanks to a goal by Romario.

title: World Cup Stadiums 1994
content: Iconic stadiums like the Rose Bowl and the Giants Stadium hosted multiple matches during the 1994 World Cup across California and New Jersey.

title: Historical Significance 1994
content: The 1994 World Cup is remembered for bringing soccer to mainstream American audiences and for Brazil matching Italy's record of four titles.
